headline: Ghana Cedi Depreciates 10.6% Against US Dollar Year-to-Date
summary: Bank of Ghana data revealed that the cedi's cumulative year-to-date depreciation reached 10.6% in November, accelerating from 9.5% in September under mounting foreign exchange pressures.
why: Cedi depreciation increases the cost of imported fuel and foodstuffs into Ghana, complicating debt restructuring and domestic inflation targets.

impacts.name: Ghanaian Cedi
impacts.why: Official data confirms accelerating depreciation against the dollar, reaching 10.6% year-to-date.
